title: Bet before the rerun
hook: How could you test whether forecasts identify replicable studies?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare forecasts recorded before replication with later outcomes rather than hindsight explanations.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare forecasts recorded before replication with later outcomes rather than hindsight explanations.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Four toy preregistered forecasts are 0.8, 0.2, 0.7 and 0.3; outcomes are 1, 0, 1 and 0. What is their mean squared-error score? Toy inputs A=[0.8, 0.2, 0.7, 0.3]; B=[0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[0.065, 0.25, 4], [0.25, 0.25, 2]]. Labels: Mean Brier score, Chance score, Correct labels.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Recording forecasts before the reruns permits an out-of-sample scoring rule. The comparison is an uninformative probability benchmark. Later explanations do not replace a dated forecast, and performance on these four cases does not establish universal forecasting skill.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Forecast 1=0.5, Forecast 2=0.5, Forecast 3=0.5, Forecast 4=0.5. What is Mean Brier score? Answer: 0.25.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Forecast 1=0.5, Forecast 2=0.5, Forecast 3=0.5, Forecast 4=0.5. What is Mean Brier score?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0.25. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.section: 25. Famous findings that failed to replicate or shrank
sourceProvenance.text: Researchers betting in prediction markets forecast which studies would replicate better than chance (Dreber et al., 2015).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare forecasts recorded before replication with later outcomes rather than hindsight explanations.
